name: Cafe des Arts
signature_dish: French breakfast — crepes, croissants and coffee in a Franco-Tamil heritage house
why_it_matters: Opened 2009 in an old Franco-Tamil house on Rue Suffren in the French Quarter — Cafe des Arts turned a historic colonial home into a whimsical Parisian-style cafe with vintage furniture and a courtyard. It is the most photographed cafe in Pondicherry and the default spot for a leisurely French breakfast in White Town.
insider_tip: Come for breakfast or mid-morning — it gets crowded and only opens roughly 9am-6pm, closed some weekdays. The crepes and the courtyard seating are the draw. Cash + cards; expect a wait in season.

name: Baker Street
signature_dish: Croissants and pain au chocolat from an eight-generation French baking family
why_it_matters: A French bakery created in 2008 on Rue Bussy, run on the recipes of a family of French bakers since 1788 — Baker Street is consistently called the best French bakery in Pondicherry and ranks #1 among the city's bakeries on TripAdvisor. The croissants and pain au chocolat are the reason it is on every Pondy food list.
insider_tip: Buy croissants and macarons fresh in the morning before they sell out. Pricey by Indian standards but the baking is genuinely French. There are two Rue Bussy shops plus a Beach Road outlet. Cash + cards.

name: Surguru
signature_dish: South Indian dosas — the dosa varieties Surguru is best known for
why_it_matters: A long-running pure-vegetarian South Indian restaurant on Mission Street, part of the Hotel Surguru group — the reliable Indian-food counterpoint to White Town's French and continental cafes. Locals and travellers rate it for some of the best dosas in town at honest prices, in a clean air-conditioned setting.
insider_tip: When you have had enough croissants and French breakfasts, this is the place for a proper South Indian dosa-and-filter-coffee meal. The dosa range is the order. Cash + cards + UPI.

name: Villa Shanti
signature_dish: French and modern Indian plates in a restored colonial mansion courtyard
why_it_matters: A fine-dining restaurant inside a restored heritage hotel on Rue Suffren in White Town — Villa Shanti is one of Pondicherry's top tables for an upscale evening, serving French and North Indian cooking in an atmospheric colonial-mansion courtyard. The go-to address for a special dinner in the French Quarter.
insider_tip: Book ahead for dinner, especially weekends — the courtyard tables are the ones to ask for. The most polished fine-dining experience in White Town if you want one celebratory meal. Cash + cards.

name: Tanto Trattoria Pizzeria
signature_dish: Wood-fired pizza on organic spelt dough with kitchen-garden toppings
why_it_matters: An Italian restaurant and pizzeria using organic spelt dough, extra-virgin olive oil and produce from its own kitchen garden — Tanto is Pondicherry's best-known address for genuine wood-fired pizza, set in a leafy garden. It runs branches in White Town and Auroville.
insider_tip: Order the wood-fired pizza on spelt crust — the organic, no-canned-ingredients approach is what sets Tanto apart. The garden setting is pleasant in the evening; book in season. Cash + cards.

name: Coromandel Cafe
signature_dish: Continental and French plates in a heritage pink-mansion garden
why_it_matters: A cafe set in a restored pink colonial mansion in White Town, with garden seating under the trees — Coromandel Cafe is a regular on Pondicherry's must-visit cafe lists, valued as much for the heritage-house setting as for its continental and French menu.
insider_tip: Best in the evening when the garden is lit — a relaxed spot for a long coffee or light dinner. The pink-mansion courtyard is the reason to come. Cash + cards.
